chapter: Sam Morgan, repertoire and Silver Leaf
title: Violins in New Orleans bands
summary: Violin was used only when a clarinet or sax was unavailable; bands relied on trumpet and clarinet.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Well, they used to use violin, sometimes they would need an extra man and they couldn't get a clarinet or a saxophone, then they would use violin. A lot of bands didn't like to use a violin. For what reason? Oh, they found it was too light, too soft. It didn't produce what they wanted.
They wanted some noise. But you think most reading bands use violin?
Oh yeah, yeah. They use it. Did you use violin in your band ever?
In all of them? Yeah, we used it. Not all the time. We used it.

In other words, it wasn't an instrument that you first picked. You picked that if you couldn't get somebody else. No. The instrument that I wanted to play was a violin when I pushed. No, I'm talking about when you had your band. You didn't feel it was necessary to get a violin. Oh no, no, no, no. You get somebody else.
You didn't think you needed a violin.
